question: Are the bytes in the downloaded archive exactly the bytes of the pinned git revision, or merely something that looks like them?

method.step1: Extract archive-1.tar.gz into a scratch directory and confirm it unpacks to exactly one top-level root.
method.step2: Walk the extracted tree and classify every entry as file, directory, symlink or special.
method.step3: Hash each regular file as a git blob object — sha1 over the literal bytes "blob <length>\0" followed by the file content — which is the same object id git itself would compute.
method.step4: Compare each computed blob id against the sha the recursive git tree records for that same path, and check the path sets in both directions.
method.step5: Emit a normalized manifest of "<path> <blobsha> <bytes>" lines, sorted, and digest it, so the whole reconciliation collapses to one comparable number.
method.whyBlobLevelNotArchiveLevel: An archive digest proves the download was not corrupted in transit. It does not prove the archive corresponds to the pinned tree. Hashing each file as a git object anchors the acquired bytes to the revision's own object ids.

archive.secondFetchNote: archive-2.tar.gz was fetched independently and matched archive-1.tar.gz on both length and sha256, so the server returned a stable representation.
